paragraphs: ASLdeafined is a subscription site for learning American Sign Language, built around a library of more than three hundred lessons. Subscribers can also search a video dictionary of more than eighteen thousand signed words. Lesson plans are grouped by audience, among them hearing parents of deaf children.

Each subscriber gets a personal progress record. A saved word list keeps the signs a learner has looked up. One subscription covers the website and a mobile app the company says is in the Apple and Google Play stores. Pricing is stated as twelve dollars a year for people at an educational institution and thirty-six dollars a year for everyone else.

The founder is described as a nationally certified interpreter who has worked with Deaf children for fifteen years. Staff listed on the same page include a library sales and program manager. Among the testimonials the site publishes is one from a public safety officer. The FAQ states that personal information is never sold or given to another company.

quote.text: You now have the capability to search over 18,000 + video words.
